# Sample coordinate research

This note accompanies `src/data/parkCoordinates.reference.json`. It is **reference material only**. The running app should keep using the supplied sample dataset (`src/data/parks.sample.json` / `assets/parks.sample.json`). These researched points are for a potential later fix; they are not wired into the UI, map, or tests.

Research was done on 24 Nov 2026 (afternoon, America/Chicago).

## Method

1. Read the twelve records in the sample JSON (id, name, sample lat/lng, address).
2. Search OpenStreetMap [Nominatim](https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/) for each park name in New York City, then reverse-geocode every sample point to see what is actually there. Requests used User-Agent `GranicusFindAPark-CoordResearch/1.0` and were spaced at least one second apart.
3. Cross-check names and locations against [NYC Parks](https://www.nycgovparks.org/) facility and park pages and, where a well-known park matched, published Wikipedia coordinates.
4. Geocode sample addresses when they were specific enough (for example `Riverside Drive, New York, NY 10024`). An address geocode is **not** a verified park location.
5. **Do not invent coordinates.** If there is no exact named park and no plausible real-world match supported by the sample address, `verified` is `null`.

Match confidence values in the JSON:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `exact named park` | A real park exists under this name (or a standard official name that is the same park). |
| `plausible real-world match by address` | The sample name is not official, but the sample address (and nearby point) identify a real park. |
| `address geocode` | A street or intersection was geocoded; it is not a verified park location. |
| `no real match found` | No defensible NYC park or unique address point; `verified` is `null`. |

Vague street-only addresses (`Shore Pkwy`, `Ridge Rd`, `Creek Rd`, `Cedar Hill Rd`, `Hillcrest Ave`) were left ungeocoded when Nominatim could not return a unique, relevant NYC result. A multi-mile parkway or a street name that exists in several boroughs is not a single point.

## Results at a glance

| id | name | Sample | Verified | Confidence | Distance / note |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| prospect-park | Prospect Park | 40.6602, -73.969 | 40.66167, -73.97083 | exact named park | 0.23 km; acreage also matches |
| riverside-commons | Riverside Commons | 40.8009, -73.9722 | 40.80417, -73.97000 | plausible match by address (Riverside Park) | 0.41 km; name is fictional |
| cedar-hill-nature-preserve | Cedar Hill Nature Preserve | 40.7128, -74.006 | *null* | no real match found | Generic NYC / City Hall point |
| sunset-playground | Sunset Playground | 40.6452, -74.0121 | 40.6477241, -74.0044270 | plausible match by address (Sunset Park Playground) | 0.71 km |
| highland-dog-park | Highland Dog Park | 40.6789, -73.9442 | *null* | no real match found | Highland Park is 4.85 km east; not used |
| veterans-memorial-field | Veterans Memorial Field | 40.7282, -73.7949 | *null* | no real match found | Memorial Dr not found in ZIP 11367 |
| old-mill-botanical-garden | Old Mill Botanical Garden | 40.6215, -74.0776 | *null* | no real match found | Address not in NYC |
| lakeshore-point | Lakeshore Point | 40.5795, -73.9707 | *null* | no real match found | Shore Pkwy too vague; sample is residential |
| east-ridge-trailhead | East Ridge Trailhead | 40.8501, -73.8662 | *null* | no real match found | Sample is a Bronxdale residential block |
| central-plaza-green | Central Plaza Green | 40.7549, -73.984 | *null* | no real match found | 0.13 km from Bryant Park; name/address do not match, so not used |
| willow-creek-wetlands | Willow Creek Wetlands | 40.6001, -74.0899 | *null* | no real match found | Willowbrook Park is 5.78 km west; not used |
| hillcrest-skate-park | Hillcrest Skate Park | 40.6934, -73.9876 | *null* | no real match found | Sample is the Brooklyn Bridge Marriott |

Only **Prospect Park** is an exact named match. **Riverside Commons** and **Sunset Playground** are plausible address matches to Riverside Park and Sunset Park Playground. The other nine names appear fictional or otherwise unmatched in NYC.

## The Cedar Hill finding

The sample coordinates for Cedar Hill Nature Preserve are exactly `40.7128, -74.006` — the textbook “New York City” point, commonly used as a stand-in for the city (New York City Hall / Lower Manhattan).

A Nominatim reverse geocode of that point returns **New York City Hall, 260 Broadway**, about 8 meters away. The address field is only `Cedar Hill Rd`, which does not identify a unique NYC street.

There is no NYC Parks site named Cedar Hill Nature Preserve. Two easy false friends were checked and rejected:

- A private **Cedar Hill Nature Preserve** in Milam County, Texas, is a different place and is not used.
- **Cedar Hill** in Central Park is a lawn, not a 212-acre nature preserve on Cedar Hill Road, and is not used.

This record is the clearest placeholder in the sample set: the map will drop a marker on City Hall unless a later fix replaces the point.

## Sources for the three matched parks

- Prospect Park: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prospect_Park_(Brooklyn)) (40°39′42″N 73°58′15″W = 40.66167, -73.97083); [NYC Parks](https://www.nycgovparks.org/parks/prospect-park).
- Riverside Park (plausible match for Riverside Commons): [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside_Park_(Manhattan)) (40°48′15″N 73°58′12″W = 40.80417, -73.97000); [NYC Parks](https://www.nycgovparks.org/parks/riverside-park). Sample address `Riverside Dr, New York, NY 10024` geocodes along that park’s 10024 stretch of Riverside Drive.
- Sunset Park Playground (plausible match for Sunset Playground): [NYC Parks facility page](https://www.nycgovparks.org/facilities/playgrounds/52) (6th Avenue between 41st and 44th Streets, inside [Sunset Park](https://www.nycgovparks.org/parks/sunset-park), which runs 41st–44th Streets between 5th and 7th Avenues). Coordinates are the OpenStreetMap way centroid, [way/881121558](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/881121558) (40.6477241, -74.0044270).

# Find a Park

A Phase 1 scaffold for a New York City-area park finder using the 12 supplied sample records.

## Run

From the repository root, using Node.js 24 and npm:

```powershell
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open the local URL printed by Vite.

## What works

The app loads and normalizes the sample. Three labeled placeholder regions show the planned layout. The list and details share the left pane, with the map on the right. The regions stack on a narrow screen.

## Left out

Resident-facing park selection, markers, tiles, and detail content are future work. Search, filters, geolocation, accounts, a backend, and deployment are outside this phase.

## Decisions

- Both JSON files are unchanged copies of the supplied sample. The app imports `src/data/parks.sample.json`. The brief names `assets/parks.sample.json`.
- Normalization requires a nonblank ID and name, trims text, and produces empty arrays for absent amenities and images. Invalid or incomplete coordinate pairs are discarded together. The park and any usable address are retained.
- `App` owns the selected ID. Map and list receive the same collection, selected ID, and selection callback. Details receives the matching park and a close callback. Each feature can be developed in its component folder.
- Brian has two open UX decisions for the details feature: whether to omit missing fields or label them “Not provided”, and what mobile Close/Back should return to after a list or marker selection.

## Known issues

The sample image URLs are placeholders. The details feature will need to handle a failed image load as well as an empty image array. The map feature will need to handle unavailable tiles while keeping the list and details usable.

## How it was checked

- `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm run lint` passed with Node.js 24.20.0 and npm 11.19.0.
- All 18 tests passed. They cover the sample's missing values, string cleanup, invalid and boundary coordinates, and rendering the three named regions with the full collection.
- SHA-256 hashes matched for the supplied JSON and both repository copies.
- A headless Chrome check of the production build measured the panes side by side at 1280 CSS pixels and stacked at 375, with no horizontal overflow at either width.

## Time spent

Approximately 3 minutes of elapsed scaffold and verification time in this session. This excludes prior planning and subsequent feature work.

## Next steps

1. **feature/map** — Use React Leaflet and OpenStreetMap tiles. Fit bounds to valid markers, connect marker selection to details, distinguish the selected marker, and handle tile failure. The map should work without a location prompt.
2. **feature/list** — Render a count and a name-sorted semantic list of buttons. Support keyboard selection, visible focus, and an accessible current-park indication.
3. **feature/details** — Show supplied fields, humanize amenity slugs, preserve hours as written, and handle missing fields and failed images. Focus the heading on selection and support mobile Close/Back.
4. After integration, exercise both selection paths on a phone and desktop, including keyboard-only use, focus movement, image failure, and tile failure.

# Find a Park

Find a Park helps NYC residents browse 12 sample parks, select one from a list or map, and read its details. The app loads the bundled dataset in the browser and needs no backend.

## Run

Developed and checked with Node.js 24.20.0 and npm 11.19.0. For Node 20 or 22, the locked tools require at least 20.19 or 22.13, respectively. OpenStreetMap tiles need no API key.

- "'`npm install` installs the dependencies.
- `npm run dev` starts the app. Open the local URL Vite prints.
- `npm test` runs the test suite once.
- `npm run build` creates the production build. Run `npm run preview` to serve it locally.

## What works

- The map fits the parks on load. Click a marker or its **View details** popup button to select a park. The selected marker grows, and the app never requests your location.
- Tab through the alphabetical list and press Enter or Space to select a park. Keyboard focus has a visible ring. An inset bar and `aria-current` identify the selected list button.
- Selection moves focus to the details heading. **Back to list** returns focus to the selected park’s button, including after selection from the map.
- The list and details sit beside the map on desktop. At widths of 44rem or less, the panels stack.
- Photos load lazily. Failed photos disappear individually. If none remain, a single illustration has a visible **Placeholder** label and a caption explaining whether the photos failed or none were supplied.

## Architecture

`App` imports `src/data/parks.sample.json`, runs each record through `normalizePark`, and owns `selectedParkId`. `ParkList` and `ParkMap` share the same parks, selected ID, and selection callback. `App` looks up the current record for `ParkDetails`. Keeping just the ID synchronizes both selection paths and avoids stale copies or a separate store.

Each feature folder holds its component, CSS, and tests. The shared `Park` type and selection props let the features develop in parallel. The pure `parksWithCoordinates` helper is tested independently of Leaflet. Native buttons in a `<ul>` provide Tab, Enter, and Space behavior without a custom ARIA listbox.

## Decisions & assumptions

- Brian chose NYC from the sample addresses and kept the supplied JSON unchanged. The map uses the original points.
- Every park shows Hours, Address, Description, Amenities, Acreage, Rating, and Photos in that order so residents can find the same facts each time. Missing facts read “Not provided.” A missing list address reads “Address not provided.”
- Hours come first in a highlighted block and preserve the supplied wording. Free text such as “Dawn to dusk” and “24 hours” is displayed without inferring an “open now” status.
- The generated illustration carries its own label so residents can distinguish it from a park photo.

## Data quality findings

- **One exact match.** Prospect Park’s sample point is about 230 m from its reference point. Riverside Commons and Sunset Playground have plausible address matches to Riverside Park and Sunset Park Playground, respectively, under unofficial sample names.
- **Nine parks have no defensible match.** Cedar Hill Nature Preserve uses the generic NYC City Hall point (`40.7128, -74.006`). Hillcrest Skate Park lands on the Brooklyn Bridge Marriott. East Ridge Trailhead lands on a residential block in Bronxdale. The researched coordinates are reference material only. [Research notes](docs/coordinates.md) · [Reference JSON](src/data/parkCoordinates.reference.json)
- Highland Dog Park lacks an address, Old Mill Botanical Garden has a null description, and Cedar Hill has a null rating. Each gets the corresponding missing-field label. Cedar Hill and East Ridge have empty image arrays and show “No photos provided.”

## Left out

Search, filters, current location, URL deep links (`?park=id`), a backend, and deployment.

## Known issues

- All supplied photo URLs point to `images.example.com`. These placeholder URLs yield the “Photo unavailable” illustration when loading fails.
- Missing tiles leave grey areas on the map without an explanatory message. The list and details still work.
- The list is the primary keyboard path. A formal screen-reader and WCAG audit is still outstanding.
- Most sample points lack a verified park match and are unsuitable for navigation.

## How it was checked

- All 73 unit and component tests passed across six files. The list tests use `@testing-library/user-event` for Tab, Enter, and Space. Photo tests dispatch errors without using the network.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm run build` passed.
- Grok Bot reviewed each PR before merge. Review replaced a direct focus-and-click test with keyboard input, caught UTF-8 BOMs from Windows tooling, fixed a layout shift on list selection, and added focus restoration on Back.
- Brian tested the app manually on localhost.

item.text:
ParkDetails now removes each failed photo while preserving the original numbering and alt text of the remaining photos. If all photos fail or none were supplied, the panel shows **exactly one illustration** with a visible **Placeholder** label and either “Photo unavailable” or “No photos provided.” The illustration has no error handler, so an error cannot reset its `src` or create a retry loop. Selecting another park starts with fresh photo state.

| `npm run typecheck` | Passed |
| `npm run lint` | Passed |
| `npm test` | **73 tests passed across 6 files** |
| `npm run build` | Passed, 72 modules transformed |

Changed only `README.md`, `package.json`, `ParkDetails.tsx`, `ParkDetails.css`, and `ParkDetails.test.tsx`. The only package change was adding the missing `"preview": "vite preview"` script. All five files were verified as UTF-8 without a BOM. App.tsx, ParkList, ParkMap, and the sample data were untouched. No commit or push was made.

The rewritten README gives the locked tools’ Node minimums and describes sample photo failures without claiming a live network check. Brian’s manual testing, AI session details, review process, start time, and external log location are documented from the supplied project history. The automated accessibility review and total time remain open as requested.
